previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and weakness due to hypercalcemia in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He received pamidronate in clinic prior to admission, which resolved his hypercalcemia. During his stay, he was treated with a 4-day pulse of dexamethasone followed by a new regimen of dexamethasone, Velcade, and Cytoxan due to progression of myeloma. His hospital course was complicated by steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin drip and dose adjustments, and poorly controlled hypertension managed with increased diltiazem and addition of amlodipine. Acute kidney injury, likely from hypercalcemia and dehydration, improved from a creatinine of 1.7 to 1.3. Dyspnea was attributed to anemia, and he was transfused one unit of red blood cells with symptom improvement. He remained on oral vancomycin for C. diff prevention and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in oncology, endocrinology, and cardiology.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SUMMARY
=============
Mr. ___ is a ___ with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma s/p 
autologous transplant (___) and several chemotherapy 
regimens, h/o bilateral PEs, HTN, DM II who presented with 
malignant hypercalcemia, ___ on CKD, hyperglycemia, and 
weakness.

ACUTE ISSUES
============
# Malignant Hypercalcemia: Pt admitted with malignant 
hypercalcemia.  Ca ___ -> 10.0 (___).  Pt received 
pemidronate during recent admission and could not get another 
dose on admission because it had been less than a week since his 
last dose.  He was treated with IV fluids and nasal calcitonin 
with normalization.  Treatment with denosumab may be considered 
in the future.

# DM II c/b hyperglycemia: Pt has DM II and has had intermittent 
hyperglycemia.  His glucose control is likely also impacted by 
IV dexamethasone that he got in clinic on ___.  He was 
initially continued on his home regimen (25 U glargine QHS with 
ISS at meals and QHS), but required additional insulin.  ___ 
followed and assisted with his insulin regimen.  On ___, he 
was hyperglycemic to >450.  He was placed on an insulin drip for 
about 12 hours and then returned to SC insulin. He was 
instructed to check his blood sugars four times daily and to 
call his endocrinologist if his blood sugar is >180 or <80 in 
order to have his insulin adjusted. He was scheduled to follow 
up with endocrinology as an outpatient the week following 
discharge.

# ___ on CKD: Cr at baseline is 1.1-1.2.  Cr on admission 1.3, 
but increased to 1.7 ___.  He was treated with IVF and his 
creatinine was trended.  Nephrotoxins were avoided and 
medications were renally dosed.

#Shortness of breath: During his course, he c/o dyspnea on 
exertion and fatigue. Because he received several liters of IVF, 
it is possible that his SOB is due to iatrogenic volume 
overload. a CXR did show mild pulmonary edema. His fluids were 
held, however his SOB did not improve significantly - he later 
reported that his DOE is chronic, however. Because of his 
history of PE, a V/Q scan was performed which showed a low 
likelihood of PE. An EKG showed no evidence of ischemia, however 
the patient should undergo an outpatient stress test given his 
cardiac risk factors. An order was placed for a pharmacologic 
stress test at ___ and the patient was encouraged to call to 
schedule an appointment.

# Refractory IgA Lambda Multiple Myeloma: Disease appeared to be 
advancing despite previous autologous transplant and several 
chemotherapy regimens.  At this time, he is receiving therapy 
with IV fluids, bortezemib, dexamethasone.  Increasing total 
protein suggested that disease was progressing.  He continued on 
IV fluids.

# Hypertension: During last hospitalization, diltiazem dose was 
increased, carvedilol was continued, and amlodipine was started. 
 Continued diltiazem, carvedilol, amlodipine.

# C difficile infection: Continued vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
===================
- The patient should undergo an outpatient cardiac stress test 
given that he is experiencing dyspnea on exertion and has 
cardiac risk factors. An order was placed in WebOMR and the 
patient was encouraged to call to schedule the appointment. 
Please ensure that the patient goes for follow-up
- The patient will need to follow up with Dr. ___, 
___ as above for further insulin management
- Consider denosumab as an outpatient given that the patient is 
experiencing recurrent hyperglycemia
